description: Challenge issuance helper lifecycle (SPEC-v2 Part B, §7.3). Each scenario replays steps in order against one issuance store and one Part B claim store that share the authoritative clock; the issuer's random source yields random_b64 in order. The helper validates the request, reads the authoritative clock as issued_at, draws 32 bytes, durably persists the complete ExpectedChallengeV2 keyed by (verifier_namespace, replay_epoch, ChallengeClaimDigest), and only then returns it. A key conflict draws fresh bytes (at most three attempts) and never overwrites a record.

operations.issue: set the clock to at; arm persist_fault for this call only (ok; fail_before_commit = nothing stored and an error; fail_after_commit = the record is stored, then an error, modelling a crash before the response); issue request. expected_agent names a keys.json fixture whose ID and complete key are bound. expect.result issued gives the exact challenge, issued_at and expires_at; error means no challenge was returned. records_after is the number of stored records after the step
operations.load: retrieve the record for challenge_b64 by ChallengeClaimDigest under the fixture namespace and epoch. expect.result found returns a record naming exactly these bytes; expected_challenge_unavailable otherwise
operations.present: set the clock to at; load the record for the bundle's challenge (expected_challenge_unavailable when absent), then run pre-claim checks (§6.2) at now = at with max_challenge_age_seconds 300, future_skew_seconds 5, required_scope data:read, the fixture namespace and epoch, and a context policy derived from the record (the Verify session-context policy with the record's expected session context when it has one, otherwise an explicit not-required policy), then the atomic claim. expect.result preflight gives the class; claimed gives the claim disposition
operations.present_concurrent: set the clock to at; present every bundle in bundles_b64 concurrently. expect.dispositions is the sorted multiset of outcomes: created, in_progress (an exact retry while evaluating), or proof_conflict (a different proof for the claimed challenge). Exactly one presentation creates the claim

scenarios.name: issue_then_present
scenarios.description: a persisted challenge is retrievable by its claim digest, claims once, and an exact retry is a replay

scenarios.name: crash_after_commit_before_exposure
scenarios.description: the store committed but the issuer failed before returning: no challenge is exposed; the orphan record is harmless and the next issuance draws fresh bytes

scenarios.name: crash_before_commit
scenarios.description: persistence failed before commit: no challenge is exposed and nothing is retrievable

scenarios.name: duplicate_issuance_never_overwrites
scenarios.description: a repeated random value conflicts with the stored record; the issuer draws again and the first record keeps its original times

scenarios.name: random_source_repeats
scenarios.description: three consecutive key conflicts fail issuance instead of looping or overwriting

scenarios.name: invalid_request
scenarios.description: an issuance request outside its bounds is configuration_invalid and draws no randomness

scenarios.name: wrong_binding
scenarios.description: the record's authenticated bindings are enforced before claim; no rejected presentation consumes the challenge

scenarios.name: expiry
scenarios.description: a challenge is fresh only while now < expires_at

scenarios.name: concurrent_claims
scenarios.description: concurrent presentations of one issued challenge: exactly one creates the claim; an identical proof is an in-progress retry and a different proof is a conflict
